title: Let go, iv
logline: Thursday. The lamp. It's his — he brought it in 2004 when the shop's died. The Owner says take it. He says it's the shop's. She says it's never been the shop's. The strip settles it by drawing it on his side of the counter.

panels.composition: The shop. The green swing-arm lamp clamped to the work bench. WOOD under it. The OWNER.

balloons.text: You brought it in '04. I remember. I remember everything.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, a thin man working under a green swing-arm lamp clamped to a bench in a frame shop, an older woman speaking to him

panels.composition: The lamp. The clamp. A scratch on the shade from 2004.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, close-up of a green enamel swing-arm lamp's shade with an old scratch, clamped to a workbench

panels.composition: Wood looking at the lamp. The lamp on his side of the counter now — the strip has moved it, quietly, between panels.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, a thin man looking at a green lamp that now stands on his side of a counter, no words
image.notes: The lamp changes sides between panels 2 and 3. Nobody moved it.

panels.composition: The Owner, back at the cutter, not looking up. Wood, the lamp, the dog. Tomorrow the last mat.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, an older woman at a mat cutter not looking up, a thin man with a green lamp and an old dog, quiet
image.notes: Her third 'Arthur' in the shop — the characters sheet says twice; the strip lets this one be the goodbye.

art.line: brush-pen; the flats cleaner; the Sundays the point now

notes: The lamp changes sides between panels. 'They always are.'
